chapter: Nonet, later partnerships and recent projects
title: Gerry Mulligan's quartet with Chet Baker
summary: He was pleased to be included in the Mulligan quartet and still gets royalties.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: What’s your overall . . . actually, we never talked about [if] we go back to fifty-three, the records you made with Mulligan’s quartet with Chet.
That was an enjoyable and unique experience. I appreciated Chet for what he was doing then. Certainly [I] was pleased with Gerry for including me in that.
I guess so. He asked me to join him at Dante’s on off nights of the Stan Kenton Band. We were at the Palladium. I think that’s the period when all of that . . .
Was it Dante’s or the Hague?
Okay. So he wrote some music to include you with the quartet right? And you made those recordings which are I guess considered classics.
I even collected a few pennies [and] royalties over the years that he very generously awarded me. I heard . . . you know Tavis Smiley?

I love this guy and he was interviewing Randy Newman and asking him about his different situations with writing hit movie scores and things like that and Randy came off being very humble and still [with] the attitude of a student learning. Still with a long way to go and everything like that. They made mention to one of his hit tunes about Los Angeles and his reaction was “Every time they play that I get two hundred and eighty-nine dollars” or something like that.
